text.p: Here are the highlights from Swiss newspapers on Friday:
- U.S. Undersecretary Stuart Eizenstat said yesterday in Zurich that the United States did not plan to start a 'vendetta' against Switzerland.

- The Swiss National Bank took in 100 tonnes of gold from the Nazis in 1943 after Sweden refused because the bullion had been stolen by Germany from Belgium, according to a Second World War document released by U.S. Senator Alfonse D'Amato on Thursday.

- Several spokesmen of leading Swiss banks said that the banks took the boycott threats serisously. The City Council of New York has a law in the making which would stop the City of New York from depositing money on Swiss bank accounts.
- Swiss chemical products maker Clariant reported a rise in sales by 192 million Swiss francs to 2.337 billion francs. Net profits are expected to rise by 15 percent.
- Swiss consumer credits declined by five percent to a total volume of 5.3 billion Swiss francs in 1996.
- Swiss President Arnold Koller opened the 27th World Economic Forum in Davos on Thursday evening. In his opening note he also addressed the question of the dormant accounts.
- Alcatel Switzerland plans to axe 470 jobs in its production plants near Zurich.
